scope: Open review of aspiration pneumonia risk factors, including dysphagia and impaired consciousness, and the microbiology of the oropharynx.

keyRecommendations.text: Oropharyngeal dysphagia is a relevant risk factor for aspiration pneumonia.
Risk factors named include impaired swallowing (dysphagia, COPD, stroke or dementia, mechanical ventilation) and impaired consciousness.
The oral environment can affect growth of potentially pathogenic anaerobic bacteria.

clinicalBottomLine: Look for dysphagia and impaired consciousness when assessing aspiration pneumonia, and do not treat the microbiology as identical to ordinary community pneumonia.
notableCaveats: The NEJM review suggested in some catalogues is not open. This PMC review is the open text used.
